body:
`dump()` makes fewer calls per string, scalar and line break. Each commit message has its own numbers.

| commit | macOS instructions |
|---|---|
| Write short plain strings and keys in one go | citm -21 %, jeopardy -17 %, twitter -10 % (vs #5878) |
| Write the scalar elements of a container without entering `dump_internal()` | -5 ... -10 % |
| Escape runs of multi-byte characters straight into the write buffer | `ensure_ascii`: CJK -56 %, twitter -32 % |
| Do not zero the serializer's buffers | small objects -6 % |
| Write the usual indentation with four stores instead of memset | -8 ... -16 % |
| Write strings and keys of up to 32 characters in one go with vectors | twitter -21 % |
| Write a line break and the indentation of the next line together | -3 ... -5 % |
| Copy the short runs between escapes as a block of 16 bytes | JSON embedded in JSON strings -10 % |
| Test strings of 8 to 15 characters as one vector | jeopardy -15 % / -7 % (Linux) |

The 256-entry table from #5878 stays as the fallback for targets without SSE2/NEON and for big-endian targets.

## Numbers

- **macOS:** at most 0.96x develop's instructions in every cell (14 corpora x output styles x `json`/`ordered_json`).
- **Linux (GCC 13 / Clang 18):** citm 0.84 / 0.81, twitter 0.78 / 0.76.
- **macOS timing:** Dump geomean 0.75, best 0.60.
- Parsing is unchanged.

## Validation

- Differential check against develop, byte-identical:
  - all error handlers, `ensure_ascii` and indents;
  - streams, deep nesting and binary values;
  - with ASan, and with `JSON_NO_SIMD`.
- 8 unit test files with ASan, in C++11 and C++20.
- All commits build on their own, and each commit's `single_include` is a fresh `make amalgamate`.

## Public API

No breaking changes: the output is byte-identical.

Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.

Yes, it was merged in #5876, and this PR should have used it. `JSON_DUMP_SHORT_STRINGS` repeated the condition of `JSON_LITTLE_ENDIAN_TARGET` word for word. It is gone in `a800ded53`, and the serializer now tests `JSON_LITTLE_ENDIAN_TARGET` directly.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

I measured it, and it is slower on object-heavy documents. I wrote all four loops (object and array, pretty and compact) in the single-loop form, with the separator or closing bracket chosen inside the loop. Instructions per `dump()`, compared with the current code:

| file | compact | pretty |
|---|---|---|
| citm_catalog.json | +1.7 % | +1.7 % |
| twitter.json | ±0 % | +1.3 % |
| canada.json | −0.2 % | −0.9 % |

Only the array-heavy canada.json gains anything, so I kept the peeled last element. (The snippet as written also needs `size()` rather than `size() - 1` as the loop bound; otherwise the last member is never written.)

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Right: in compact mode it is always 0 and is only read by `dump_binary_value()` when pretty-printing. The compact paths now pass `0` (`a800ded53`).

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Same as at https://github.com/nlohmann/json/pull/5883#discussion_r4350238741: putting `,` vs `}` (and `,` vs `]`) in the loop costs up to 1.7 % on object-heavy files, so the loops stay as they are.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Done in `a800ded53`. `dump()` was the only other caller, and it now goes through `dump_element()` too. The function is renamed to `dump_container()`, asserts that it gets an object or an array, and tests the depth limit once before an `if` on object vs array. The scalar cases are gone. Instruction counts are unchanged or slightly lower.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Half done: it is called only for keys, so it is now `put_object_key()` (`a800ded53`). I kept the tail as an argument. Every caller already sits on the pretty-printing or the compact branch, so the tail is a constant there and `put_short_quoted()` gets a fixed length. Choosing it inside would either test `pretty_print` again for every key or inline the fast path twice. The doc comment now says why.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Yes, a leftover: develop wrapped it because the line was `val.m_data.m_value.binary->cbegin()`. Both binary loops are on one line now (`a800ded53`).

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Right, all three places in `dump_binary_value()` now use `put_literal_indent()`, and so do the two closing brackets in `dump_iteratively()` (`a800ded53`).

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Agreed, it is `#if !JSON_LITTLE_ENDIAN_TARGET || !JSON_SCAN_VECTOR` now (`a800ded53`).

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Done in `a800ded53`: `bool put_short_literal_indent()` holds the fast path, and `put_indent()` calls it with `""`. The length is a compile-time constant, so a `memcpy` of 0 bytes compiles to nothing and no `if (length == 0)` is needed. That is good, since MSVC would warn about such a constant condition (C4127). Instruction counts are unchanged.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

No. Only bytes of 0x80 and above get here, and `validate_one_utf8()` returns 2 to 4 for those, or 0 for an invalid sequence, which ends the loop just above. `a800ded53` adds a `JSON_ASSERT(length >= 2 && length <= 4)` and marks the `default:` as the 4-byte case.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Yes, essentially. `-Weffc++` wants every member in the constructor's initializer list, and for a plain `std::array`, `number_buffer()` there means value-initialization, i.e. zeroing 1.6 KiB on every `dump()`. With an empty user-provided default constructor, the same initializer does nothing. The alternative is to leave the buffers out of the list and silence `-Weffc++` with pragmas for GCC. The empty constructor keeps the intent at the type and needs no compiler-specific code.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*
Thanks for the detailed confirmation.

         write_buffer_pos += length;
     }
 
+    /*!
+    @brief append the characters of @a str in [@a start, @a start + @a length)
+
+    A run of up to 16 characters with 16 or more in the string from @a start on
+    and in the write buffer from its end on is copied as a whole block of 16,
+    which spares the call of memcpy with a length known only at run time; the
+    surplus characters in the buffer are overwritten by what follows.
+    */
+    template<typename StringType>
+    void put_run(const StringType& str, const std::size_t start, const std::size_t length)
+    {
+        // a short run is the exception in text without escapes (CJK, accented
+        // Latin), for which this keeps the long path the fast one
+        if (JSON_HEDLEY_UNLIKELY(length <= 16 && start + 16 <= str.size() && write_buffer_pos + 16 <= write_buffer.size()))
+        {
+            std::memcpy(write_buffer.data() + write_buffer_pos, str.data() + start, 16);
